plan.title: Agent MCP and bots (W-OAUTH2): OAuth in the dashboard: approval card and sign-in list

metadata.fileOverlapNote: scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt is merge=union; parallel items that each append one test path do not conflict, so no edge is added for it.

narratives.Problem: W-OAUTH1 (PAN-4945) shipped the OAuth 2.1 server for /mcp. A client that signs in waits on a public authorize page showing an approval code, and the operator can approve it only with `pan mcp oauth approve <code>` in a terminal. Active sign-ins are visible only through `pan mcp oauth list`, and agent tokens (one per running agent) flood the dashboard's token lists.
narratives.Proposal: Frontend only. Add frontend OAuth types, a level mirror and fetchers to anywhereApi.ts; feed each pending approval into useDecisions as a blocking `mcpSignIn` decision (root viewers only) rendered by a new McpSignInCard in the Needs-you panel (code, redirect host, level select, Approve, Deny); add a McpSignInsList (client, level, created, last used, expires, Revoke) mounted in both Settings → Access Tokens and Settings → Anywhere → Access tokens; fold agent tokens behind 'Show agent tokens (N)' in both token lists; document it. Every call goes to the existing root-only /api/mcp-oauth/* routes.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No server route, route-scope row, no-loss row, CLI verb, config key or src/lib change; the diff stays in src/dashboard/frontend/src/, scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt and docs
- No approving from a phone, a paired device or a linked machine's dashboard; those viewers never see the card's controls
- No desktop, push or TTS notification for a new sign-in
- No editing a sign-in's level after approval
- No hiding OAuth access tokens (oauthClientId records) from the token lists; only agent tokens fold
- No widening of PendingInputSource ('agent' | 'conversation')
- No token, refresh token or code verifier ever reaches the browser

autoDecisions.summary: Mount the Sign-ins list in both Settings → Access Tokens (AccessTokensSection) and Settings → Anywhere → Access tokens (AccessTokensPanel).
autoDecisions.rationale: AC-17 names Settings → Access Tokens (the separate section, settingsPageConstants.ts:64) while the epic's file list names AccessTokensPanel; the token list already appears in both on one shared query key, so mirroring that precedent satisfies both inputs.

autoDecisions.summary: The mcpSignIn kind is blocking and labelled 'MCP sign-in waiting'.
autoDecisions.rationale: A person is parked on the authorize page and the request expires in 10 minutes, so it belongs with the blocking rows that sort first.

autoDecisions.summary: The approvals query runs only for viewer kinds 'root-session' and 'internal-token'.
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic says root session; the internal token is also a root credential the admin routes accept. The gate only avoids a 403 poll; the server's root check is the boundary.
That is when the sign-in itself ends unless the client refreshes; the 30-day access token rotates on every refresh.

autoDecisions.summary: OAuth access tokens stay visible in the token lists; only agentId records fold.
autoDecisions.rationale: configuration/mcp.mdx:323-325 (W-OAUTH1) already documents revoking an OAuth access token there; the epic asks only for agent tokens to be hidden.

autoDecisions.summary: Frontend OAuth types, level labels and fetchers live in anywhereApi.ts as a mirror of src/lib/mcp/oauth-flow.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: oauth-flow.ts imports node:crypto so the frontend cannot import it; anywhereApi.ts already mirrors MCP_DEFAULT_SCOPES the same way and is the epic's named file.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. After MCP_DEFAULT_SCOPES (anywhereApi.ts:90) add MCP_OAUTH_LEVELS, McpOAuthLevel, MCP_OAUTH_LEVEL_LABELS (comment: mirrors LEVEL_LABELS in src/lib/mcp/oauth-flow.ts), isMcpOAuthLevel, McpSignInApproval and McpSignIn interfaces (mirrors of PendingApprovalView and SignInView in src/lib/mcp/oauth-service.ts:68-89; requestedLevel and level typed string), MCP_OAUTH_APPROVALS_QUERY_KEY = ['mcp-oauth-approvals'], MCP_SIGN_INS_QUERY_KEY = ['mcp-oauth-sign-ins'], and four fetchers: fetchMcpSignInApprovals(signal) (GET /api/mcp-oauth/approvals, [] on any failure), decideMcpSignIn(id, 'approve'|'deny', level?) Ids are encodeURIComponent'd; mutations send await dashboardMutationJsonHeaders(). Reuse readResult/isOk/apiError. New test mcpOAuthApi.test.ts (mock ../../../../lib/wsTransport as AccessTokensPanel.test.tsx:10-12 does), listed in scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt in sorted position.
